reason: The cited evidence shows elastic isotropy and weak temperature-dependent elastic anisotropy in NbTaTiV (E1), but provides no data on HfNbTaTiZr, no evidence for edge dislocation super-jogging, and no support for the claimed plateaus in strength, moduli, or lattice strain. The second passage (E2) concerns nano-indentation creep in different alloys and is unrelated to the key premises.
premises: Elastic isotropy is retained at elevated temperatures in HfNbTaTiZr
Edge dislocation super-jogging is activated and inhibits dislocation motion at 873–1073 K
Super-jogging and elastic isotropy together cause a plateau in yield strength and elastic moduli
Lattice strain evolution becomes temperature-insensitive in the 873–1073 K range
These behaviors are atypical compared to conventional BCC alloys
